fields.h1: Build a Language Quiz for Any Language and Level
fields.hero_description: Build a language quiz in any language that scores each player, places them by level, and saves answers to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Language Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A language quiz checks what someone knows about a language or about languages. Emergent builds the quiz and the table behind it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions in the language you teach

Name the language, the level, and the topic, such as Spanish verbs in the past tense. Emergent writes each question with one right answer and three wrong ones of the same kind.
fields.feature_2:
Score bands that place each learner

Set the bands, such as 0 to 9 for Level 1 and 10 to 17 for Level 2, and the quiz shows each player the level they land in. Ask Emergent to draft the message for each band.
fields.feature_3:
Every answer tagged by skill

Each answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the player, the question, and the skill it tests, such as verbs or vocabulary. Sort by skill to see what a class misses.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Players answer one question per screen, so a class can take the quiz on their phones in the first ten minutes of a lesson. Emergent puts no cap on how many people answer a quiz.
fields.feature_5:
A list of who fell below the pass mark

Set a pass mark, such as 12 of 15, and the app posts the name of anyone below it to a Slack channel. Send the list by email instead when only one teacher or trainer needs to see it.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and your own code

Publish the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and add next term's questions.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Run a Language Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
Of 58 new students, 27 placed into Level 2

Bracewell Language School sends a 24-question French placement quiz to every adult who signs up for fall. Scores of 0 to 9 place a student in Level 1, 10 to 17 in Level 2, and 18 to 24 in Level 3. Each result is saved with the student and level. Level 2 got 27 of the 58, so the school opened a second Tuesday section.
fields.tab_content_2:
For the imperfect question, 19 of 31 picked wrong

Every Thursday, the Spanish 2 class at Greywater High takes a 12-question past-tense quiz on their phones, one question per screen. The app stores every answer by student and by question. This week, 19 of 31 students missed question 7, the only one on the imperfect, and the teacher opened Friday's class with it.
fields.tab_content_3:
By Sunday, Icelandic had fooled 289 of 340

The Oakhaven Folk Festival ran a guess-the-language booth for a weekend. Each of the 10 questions showed a sentence, and visitors picked its language from 4 options. Of 340 visitors, 299 named the Spanish sentence, but only 51 named the Icelandic one. The festival booked an Icelandic storyteller for next year.
fields.tab_content_4:
After week one, 4 of 14 hires are posted to Slack

Lantern Quay Hotel gives each new front-desk hire a 15-question quiz on the Spanish phrases guests use at check-in. Anyone who scores under 12 of 15 is posted to #frontdesk-training in Slack. This month that was 4 of 14 new hires, and each one practices check-in with a Spanish-speaking supervisor for a shift.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Language Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a language quiz with fair questions and a results table that shows what to teach next.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the score is for
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show a reason after each answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: A placement quiz sorts people into levels, a class quiz checks one unit, and a guess-the-language quiz is for fun. Pick one before writing. Put it in your prompt with the language and the audience, and Emergent drafts questions at that level.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Label every question with one skill: verb tenses, vocabulary, or reading a short sentence. Keep at least three questions per skill. Those labels are what let the results table show which skill a class needs more time on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write the correct answer, then three wrong ones a real learner would pick, such as the preterite form when the sentence needs the imperfect. A wrong option in another language, or a made-up word, gives the answer away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Under each question, add one line that explains the answer, such as the rule behind a verb ending or the clue inside a sentence. Players read it on the results screen, and a teacher can point to it when a student asks why.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Fix the level bands before launch
fields.howto_step_5_des: For a placement quiz, decide the score range for each level, such as 0 to 5, 6 to 11, and 12 to 15 on a 15-question quiz. Check that every possible score lands in exactly one level, then write what each level means.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it on a beginner and a native
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before launch, ask one beginner and one native speaker to play. A native speaker who misses a question has found a badly worded one. A beginner who gets everything right has found options that give the answer away.
fields.howto_step_7_des: After the first round, sort the table by skill and by question. Open the next lesson or training shift with the two questions missed most, then run the same quiz again a month later and compare the two rounds.

faq_plan.a: A language quiz is a short set of questions that checks what a person knows about one language, such as its verbs and words. Some ask about languages in general instead, such as which family a language belongs to. Teachers use one to check a unit or to place new students, and a festival booth can run one for fun.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a language quiz?
faq_plan.a: Describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: the language, how many questions, and what the score should do. Emergent sets up the questions, the scoring, and a database for every answer. Play it once yourself, then change any question by prompt before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: How do you write language quiz questions for beginners?
faq_plan.a: Use only words and sentences from the units the class has covered, and keep each question to one short sentence. Ask learners to recognize before they produce: picking the right word from four comes before typing it. Put the instructions in the learner's first language. That way the question tests the language and not the directions.

faq_plan.q: What makes good language quiz questions and answers?
faq_plan.a: Good language quiz questions and answers test one point each, such as a verb ending or the meaning of a word, and the answer key names the rule instead of a letter. Save the exceptions for a later round, once the rule itself is solid. A love language quiz works differently: it has no right answers, and each option points to a result instead of a score.

faq_plan.q: Can a language quiz place students into levels automatically?
faq_plan.hint: What are the 5 love languages quiz?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Set a score range for each level, and the quiz shows each student their level the moment they finish. Emergent builds the bands from your prompt. The app saves each placement with the student's name, and the school can watch every class list fill before term starts.

faq_plan.q: How do you make a guess-the-language quiz?
faq_plan.hint: What are the five love languages quiz?
faq_plan.a: Show one sentence per question and offer four languages as options. Mix easy pairs with hard ones: Spanish against Japanese is easy, while Spanish against Portuguese, or Danish against Norwegian, makes players read closely. Use a sentence with the same meaning in every language, such as a greeting. Then the spelling and the script are the only clues.

faq_plan.q: Should a language quiz use multiple choice or typed answers?
faq_plan.hint: What is my love language quiz buzzfeed?
faq_plan.a: Use multiple choice to test recognition and typed answers to test spelling and recall. A typed question needs a list of every spelling you accept, including versions without accent marks, or correct answers get marked wrong. Start beginners on multiple choice and add typed questions as the course goes on.

faq_plan.q: How long should a language quiz be?
faq_plan.hint: What is my love language quiz free?
faq_plan.a: Match the length to the job. A check at the start of class works at 10 to 12 questions, which fit in about ten minutes. A placement quiz needs more, around 20 to 30. That gives each level several questions of its own, and one lucky guess cannot move a student up.

faq_plan.q: How do you track language quiz results over a whole term?
faq_plan.a: Save every answer with the student and the skill, then compare each round with the one before. Emergent keeps a full term of quizzes in one table, inside a database you own. Sort it by skill to see whether past tenses improved after you retaught them.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a language quiz with next year's class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep the quiz and swap the questions by prompt, or add a new unit while last year's results stay in the table. On paid plans, Emergent exports the quiz's code to your GitHub repository, where a school developer can host it or change it.

quiz.title: Language Quiz: 8 Questions on Alphabets and Language Families
quiz.intro: Eight questions on alphabets, language families, and one invented language. Pick one answer for each; your score and a source for every answer show at the end.

questions.text: Which of these is one of the six official languages of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The six are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish.

source.quote: These are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.

questions.text: The alphabet called Hangul is the writing system for which language?
questions.explanation: Hangul is the Korean alphabet, the modern writing system for Korean.

source.quote: The Korean alphabet is the modern writing system for the Korean language.

questions.text: Which language of Europe is a language isolate, related to no other known language?
questions.explanation: Basque is Europe's only known language isolate, with no relation to any other known language.

source.quote: Basque is Europe's only known language isolate (with no relation to any other known languages)

questions.text: Which of these languages belongs to the Uralic family?
questions.explanation: Hungarian is a member of the Uralic language family.

source.quote: Hungarian is a member of the Uralic language family.

questions.text: Spanish, French, and Italian descend directly from which language?
questions.explanation: The Romance languages, also called the Latin languages, descend directly from Vulgar Latin.

source.quote: less commonly known as the Latin languages, are the languages that directly descended from Vulgar Latin

questions.text: Which language did L. L. Zamenhof create in 1887 for international use?
questions.explanation: Zamenhof meant Esperanto as a universal second language for international communication.

source.quote: Created by L. L. Zamenhof in 1887 as 'the International Language', it is intended to be a universal second language for international communication

questions.text: Modern Icelandic developed from which earlier language?
questions.explanation: Old Norse later became Old Icelandic, and then the Modern Icelandic spoken today.

source.quote: Icelandic is derived from an earlier language Old Norse, which later became Old Icelandic and currently Modern Icelandic.

questions.text: Swahili, spoken across East Africa, belongs to which group of languages?
questions.explanation: Swahili is a Bantu language, part of the Sabaki branch.

source.quote: Swahili is a Bantu language of the Sabaki branch.

results.title: Language Explorer
results.description: You got 0 to 3 right. Alphabets and language families are a deep subject, and every answer above names its source, so the reading list is ready.

results.title: Well Traveled
results.description: You got 4 to 6 right. You know your way around the major language families. The ones you missed are the odd cases, like a language with no relatives.

results.title: Language Expert
results.description: You got 7 or 8 right. You can place a language by its family, its alphabet, and the language it grew out of.

plan.angle: The top 10 is all play: Britannica, JetPunk, Sporcle, BuzzFeed, Speechling and guess-the-language videos offer a language quiz to take, and none shows how to make one with your own questions, levels and results table. This page gives both: an 8-question world languages quiz to play on the page, every answer sourced, then four language quizzes that a language school, a Spanish teacher, a folk festival and a hotel run as their own app, each saving every answer to a table that shows who goes where and what people missed.
